To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we introduce a new self-supervised learning approach for learning representations for embodied agents, that we learn representations by segmenting an agent’s trajectory in zones and predict features of randomly masked out zones, and that this approach obtains 2 -6× higher sample efficiency and up to 50% higher performance over image representation learning on multiple downstream tasks on the real-world 3D environments.

we introduce a novel self-supervised approach for learning environment-level visual representations for visual navigation, that we demonstrate successful transfer to downstream tasks, and that we obtain 2 - 7 times higher sample efficiency and up to 50% higher performance over state-of-the-art image-level representation learning.
1) We introduce environment predictive-coding, a self-supervision approach for learning representations of the agent’s 3D environment from a video walkthrough.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing methods for self-supervised learning of environment-level representations for visual navigation.
the development of new self-supervised learning techniques for learning environment-level representations that can be applied to embodied navigation tasks.
developing self-supervised learning methods to learn representations of the environment for visual navigation tasks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

our method is a self-supervised representation learning framework for 3D environment understanding that can be trained on video walkthroughs of a single 3D environment, and then applied to downstream tasks in unseen environments, such as goal-directed navigation and exploration.
environment predictive coding can be applied to real world scenarios to learn environment representations that can be used for navigation.
the proposed method is a self-supervised method that can learn representations of the environment from a single viewpoint and can be used for downstream tasks.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel method for self-supervised learning of environment representations that can be applied to any environment.
we propose to use the geometric and semantic structure of the environment as a self-supervised cue to learn representations that generalize to downstream tasks.
environment-level representations can be learned in a self-supervised fashion, and that such representations can improve downstream visual navigation tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
self-supervision can be extended beyond the image level and that learning environment-level representations is a promising avenue to improve sample efﬁciency in reinforcement learning.

self-supervised representation learning can be used to learn representations that capture the geometry and semantic regularities in a 3D scene, and that these representations are highly useful for downstream navigation tasks.

learning environment representations is a promising direction for self-supervised visual navigation, and that the explicit spatial conditioning of our masked-zone prediction task can help to learn more generalizable representations.
